purpose: Descriptive actual-pixel audit of the pass-5 used lower-platen contact-face correction. This is not a perceptual score, an engine ranking, or a model-benefit measurement.

method.reference_scope: Eighteen fresh LED RGB frames across task 9-14 and both cameras plus one fresh frame from every one of the 18 REF machine-camera groups were opened. Two full-resolution LED/IR frames were used for the numeric lower-platen audit.
method.roi_selection: Manual lower-platen ROIs were chosen only after opening full-resolution pixels. The views are not registered and differ in camera, crop, exposure, sensor response, compression, lighting and contamination.
method.ir_limit: IR/non-LED pixels are used only to confirm stable disc geometry, circular/radial wear, residue, debris and localized reflection. Their luminance is not an RGB material target.
method.gradient: Mean of absolute one-pixel horizontal and vertical luminance differences.
method.highpass: Mean absolute luminance difference from a 2 px Gaussian blur.
method.controlled_comparison: Blender uses camera_angled seed 54241 before/after. Unreal uses camera_angled seed 58523 before/after. Camera, sample, RFID, light and sensor decisions remain fixed; only the pass-5 lower-contact implementation and Unreal debris-height/scale correction are intended changes.
method.interpretation_limit: ROI values expose the former bright-disc error and possible over-texturing. They do not prove photorealism or establish that one engine is better.

observations: Fresh LED and every-REF IR review agree that the lower platen is a dark used-steel contact surface with circular/radial wear, concrete dust or damp residue, debris and local specular response; neither a uniformly white disc nor a flat black absorber is supported.

The controlled Blender lower-platen ROI moved from mean RGB [126.18,117.83,110.28] to [97.62,88.31,80.64], while the selected real LED dark-sector ROI is [70.34,70.22,81.51]. This closes the dominant white/clean cue but does not geometrically register the views.

The controlled Unreal ROI moved from [190.76,174.95,154.22] to [129.57,107.87,79.81]. Unreal's 2 px high-pass rose from 0.01973 to 0.03443, slightly above the selected real LED ROI's 0.02932; dense sensor/material speckle is therefore a residual over-texturing risk, not evidence of superior detail.

The inspected IR empty-chamber platen has a broad luminance distribution (median 0.38039, p90 0.89804) caused by a dark used surface plus strong localized reflection. The three bounded dry/dusty/damp regimes preserve this possibility without fitting RGB color to IR.

Unreal debris was previously generated at z=7.0-9.6 cm while the platen top is z=23.55 cm, leaving it physically below the visible contact surface. The same RNG draw is now remapped onto the platen top, with two rare larger chips and a millimetre-scale tail, so downstream sample/tag RNG decisions remain stable.

Both final contact sheets retain camera, cube/cylinder and lower-surface regime diversity. Blender remains cleaner and smoother than the real residue/wear field; Unreal remains sepia, noisy and geometrically coarse. The real upper platen, fisheye response and concrete pore/crack tail remain larger gaps than further arbitrary lower-platen darkening.
